ToolHeader.title: New Uzbek Alphabet Converter
ToolHeader.description: Convert text to the 2027 Uzbek Latin alphabet: sh → ş, ch → ç, g' → ğ, o' → ö — or from it back to the old Latin and Cyrillic. The conversion runs in your browser.

organisations.title: Is your organisation switching to the new alphabet?
organisations.description: We convert your website, documents and forms to the new alphabet in one go.
organisations.hint: Tell us on Telegram what needs converting — a website, documents or both — and roughly how much.

letters.title: The new Uzbek alphabet (2027): what changes
letters.description: The alphabet becomes 28 letters and the tutuq mark, instead of 26 letters and 3 letter combinations. Every other letter stays as it is. Click a new letter to copy it.

notes.full: The new alphabet — 28 letters and the tutuq mark: A B D E F G Ğ H I J K L M N O Ö P Q R S Ş Ç T U V X Y Z ʼ
notes.ng: Ng leaves the alphabet as a letter combination, but words are still written with n and g: yangi, köngil, dengiz.
notes.tutuq: The tutuq (the apostrophe mark) stays, in the same shape: ʼ (U+02BC) — maʼno, sanʼat.
notes.noC: No C is added: ts stays two letters — informatsiya.
notes.lookalike: Do not confuse ş with ș (U+0219, comma below): they look the same but are different letters to a computer. This tool corrects ș automatically, along with ǵ and ŏ from the 2019 and 2021 drafts.

law.title: Dates
law.programmeValue: To be approved by the Cabinet of Ministers within two months
law.spellingValue: New ones not yet published — the 1995 rules apply

keyboard.title: How to type the new letters
keyboard.description: There is no official Uzbek keyboard layout yet (October 2026). These methods work today and type the exact letters the law uses. Menu names are given as in the English interface.
keyboard.easiest: The easiest way is to type as usual — sh, ch, o', g' — and convert the text on this page. On other sites the <ext>browser extension</ext> does it: pick “New Latin”, select the text and press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>L</kbd> (on a Mac <kbd>⌘</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>L</kbd>) — the converted text is copied. If you need the letter itself:

emojiPanel.title: Emoji and symbols panel (Windows 11)
emojiPanel.body: Press <kbd>Win</kbd> + <kbd>.</kbd>, open the Ω section and pick the letter among the Latin letters. Take ş, not ș with a comma below: they are different letters.

word.title: Word: code, then Alt + X
word.body: Type the letter's code and press <kbd>Alt</kbd> + <kbd>X</kbd> right after it — the code turns into the letter. Works in WordPad too.

extended.title: The “ABC – Extended” layout
extended.body: Add it once: System Settings → Keyboard → Text Input → Edit → “+” → English → ABC – Extended. Then press the mark with <kbd>⌥</kbd>, then the letter. For a capital, press the second key with <kbd>Shift</kbd>.

abc.title: On the plain “ABC” layout
abc.body: Two work with no setup: <kbd>⌥</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd> → ç, <kbd>⌥</kbd> + <kbd>U</kbd>, then <kbd>O</kbd> → ö. ş and ğ need “ABC – Extended”.

turkish.title: Add the Turkish keyboard
turkish.body: Android (Gboard): Settings → Languages → Add keyboard → Türkçe. iPhone: Settings → General → Keyboard → Keyboards → Add New Keyboard → Türkçe. ğ, ş, ö and ç get keys of their own; switch keyboards with the language key.

dotless.title: Watch for the two i's
dotless.body: On the Turkish keyboard the dotless ı sits where i usually is, and the dotted i is next to ş. Uzbek has only the dotted i: a word typed with ı is recognised neither by search engines nor by spell-checkers.

warning.title: Don't add “Turkish Q” on a computer
warning.body: On Windows and on a Mac alike, this layout types the dotless ı on the i key, ö on the comma key and ç on the period key. The key shows a different letter, and the mistake is hard to spot in the text.

whenInForce.question: When does the new alphabet take effect?
whenInForce.answer: On 22 April 2027. Law O'RQ-1184 was signed and officially published on 21 October 2026; under Article 4 it takes effect six months after official publication. Until then the 1995 Latin alphabet remains in force.

whatChanged.question: What changes in the alphabet?
whatChanged.answer: Two letters change shape: G'g' → Ğğ, O'o' → Öö. Two letter combinations become single letters: Sh sh → Şş, Ch ch → Çç. The Ng combination leaves the alphabet, but words are still written with n and g. The tutuq mark (ʼ) stays. The result is 28 letters and one tutuq mark. No C is added.

unicode.question: What are the Unicode code points of Ş, Ç, Ğ and Ö?
unicode.answer: In the official text of the law on lex.uz: Ş U+015E and ş U+015F, Ç U+00C7 and ç U+00E7, Ğ U+011E and ğ U+011F, Ö U+00D6 and ö U+00F6; the tutuq is ʼ U+02BC. A common mistake is typing the Romanian ș (U+0219) for ş: they look the same, but to a search engine or a spell-checker they are different letters.

howToType.question: How do I type the new letters?
howToType.answer: No official Uzbek keyboard layout has been published yet (as of October 2026). The easiest way is to type as usual with o', g', sh and ch, then convert the text on this page. If you need the letter itself: on a Mac, the “ABC – Extended” layout gives ş with ⌥C, then S; in Word, type 015F, then Alt + X; on a phone, add the Turkish keyboard. Don't add “Turkish Q” on a computer: its i key types the dotless ı. Details are in the “Keyboard” section above.

oldDocuments.question: Do documents and banknotes in the old alphabet stay valid?
oldDocuments.answer: Yes. Under Article 2 of the law, documents issued in the old letters before it takes effect, the national currency and securities remain valid and in circulation. The symbols and other attributes of state bodies and organisations, the relief of the State Emblem on their buildings, signs and plates with the names of geographic features, and other items set by the Cabinet of Ministers stay in use until they wear out or until the deadline in the implementation programme.

accuracy.question: How accurate is the conversion? What about words like Isʼhoq?
accuracy.answer: Letters are replaced according to the table in the law. New spelling rules have not been adopted yet, so the 1995 rules apply: where s and h are two separate sounds, the tutuq stays between them — Isʼhoq, asʼhob. Links, e-mail addresses, code and product names (Chrome, GitHub) are left unchanged. This is not an official government tool; it will be updated when the new spelling rules are published.
